data.name: Phalgun
data.gender_notes: Phalgun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Phalgun is derived from the Sanskrit word 'phalguna', which means 'red' or 'spring'. In Hindu mythology, Phalgun is the name of the month corresponding to February in the Gregorian calendar and is associated with the god of fertility, Agni. The name Phalgun carries the meaning “Spring or Red” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Phalgun usually hope their child will grow to embody spring or red and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings, growth, and transformation.
data.etymology: Phalgun belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Spring or Red.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Phalgun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Phalgun holds significant cultural significance in various aspects of Hindu society. Throughout India, the starting of the month of Phalgun marks the onset of spring, signifying the rebirth of nature. It is an auspicious time, and numerous Hindu festivals, such as Holi and Mahashivratri, are celebrated during this month. Phalgun is also associated with various deities, like Lord Rama, Cita, Kanha, and Shiva, further emphasizing its importance in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Phalgun represents the essence of transformation and renewal. As the name signifies the arrival of spring, it is associated with the concept of renewal and rejuvenation. On a spiritual level, Phalgun encourages individuals to let go of old habits and make a transformation towards positivity and spiritual growth. The fiery and intense energy of Agni, the god of fire and the presiding deity of this month, is believed to stimulate creativity and passion to manifest one's essence and destiny.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Phalgun signifies the ripening of fruits symbolizing the maturation of inner virtues and the blossoming of spiritual wisdom in an individual. It also represents the triumph of righteousness over adversity, as the month is associated with Lord Hanuman's victory over the demon king Mahiravana.
